precedents.signature_overlap: Audit analysis daemon confirmed active and consuming CPU; security module in enforcing mode with real denials being logged — both present in INC-2288 and in the current incident.
precedents.divergence: INC-2288 fired under host.cpu.saturation, not host.memory.exhaustion; the current incident's primary signal is memory exhaustion with CPU as a secondary observation. INC-2288 was resolved by deactivating the audit event dispatcher — that resolution is superseded: Platform security standard SEC-STD-14 (2026-01-30) requires the audit event dispatcher to remain active on production hosts. Deactivating it is no longer an available resolution, and doing it here destroyed the evidence that would have identified the source domain. The source domain of the denials was never identified in INC-2288 because the dispatcher was deactivated before the denial log could be collected; the same outstanding evidence (audit denial log) is still outstanding here.
precedents.resolution_taken: Deactivated the audit event dispatcher. Daemon exited and CPU recovered. Resolution is superseded — see divergence.
precedents.falsifying_test: If the audit denial log (still outstanding) shows no elevated denial volume, the daemon's CPU consumption has a different driver and this precedent does not apply.

incident_ref.heading_path: INC-2419: Memory exhaustion closed with the cause unconfirmed

precedents.signature_overlap: Identical signature type host.memory.exhaustion; also an integration-tier host (intg-prod-j5 vs intg-prod-a1); restart was the resolution taken.
precedents.divergence: In INC-2419 the problem had auto-opened and auto-closed on seven of ten days before a restart was attempted; there is no record here of recurrence over multiple days. Critically, INC-2419 explicitly records that process-level attribution was never captured while the host was exhausted (passage p-0b2d395d47a7: 'Process-level attribution was never captured while the host was exhausted, so there is no record of what held the memory'), and the root cause was left unconfirmed. The current incident has that evidence still outstanding — the same gap that made INC-2419 unresolved. A restart here would reproduce that gap.
precedents.resolution_taken: Workload restarted. The symptom stopped; the cause was not established and no falsifying test was recorded.
precedents.falsifying_test: If process-level memory attribution is captured before any restart and shows no single dominant consumer, the INC-2419 pattern (single workload restart clears the symptom) does not transfer.

incident_ref.heading_path: INC-2411: Memory exhaustion on a batch integration host after a heap resize

precedents.signature_overlap: Identical signature type host.memory.exhaustion; integration-tier host; service restart was part of the resolution.
precedents.divergence: INC-2411 had a recent heap-resize change as the anchoring finding, and the resolution was a revert of that change followed by a restart — not a restart alone. No change history has been examined here. INC-2411 also records that no process-level attribution was captured before the revert, leaving other consumers unmeasured (passage p-b5386e8a3c6f). The outstanding evidence request here (process-level attribution) is exactly the gap INC-2411 noted as a deficiency.
precedents.resolution_taken: Reverted the heap change and restarted the integration service outside the batch window. Confirmed by the swap curve returning to its pre-change baseline within the hour.
precedents.falsifying_test: If change history for intg-prod-a1 shows no recent heap or tuning change in the period before exhaustion began, the INC-2411 pattern does not transfer.
